voice_style: Read as a 1980s public-information documentary narrator: calm, dry, slightly formal. Keep a steady, slightly brisk pace with only short pauses between sentences. Say numbers clearly.

lines.text: Cancer is a word. Waiting is a number.
A computer can never be held accountable. We agree.
Each dot is a simulated patient. The piles are waiting: eighty-seven percent of the days.
A model reads the notes and suggests a fast track when immediate care is needed.
Our platform maps the whole pathway, simulates every patient, and tests a better order before anyone waits. Same machines. Fewer days lost.
Checked against a real Norwegian hospital. In Finland: eighteen to thirty-three percent, with no new equipment.
We propose a research-based framework for future automation. A doctor decides every case.
